title: NFPA 70E, Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace (NFPA overview page)
summary: NFPA describes 70E as requirements for safe work practices that protect personnel by reducing exposure to major electrical hazards, originally developed at OSHA's request, helping avoid injuries and fatalities from shock, electrocution, arc flash, and arc blast, and assisting compliance with OSHA workplace electrical rules. Motivates EL02 as a text classification of reported hazard signs; the standard, not the label, governs practice.

title: NFPA 70, National Electrical Code (NFPA overview page)
summary: NFPA describes NFPA 70, the National Electrical Code, as enforced in all 50 states and the benchmark for safe electrical design, installation, and inspection to protect people and property from electrical hazards, with edition, amendment, and errata records. Motivates EL01, EL03, EL04, EL07; no article is cited and no rule is applied by the model.

title: Wikipedia: Residual-current device
summary: Describes ground-fault protective devices such as GFCIs as distinct from overcurrent devices. Motivates EL07 as a device-type classification; encyclopedic overview.

title: Washington State L&I: Electrical Permits, Fees & Inspections
summary: A jurisdiction's public description of when electrical permits are required, fees, and inspections, including reinspection after corrections. Motivates EL03, EL04, EL05, EL06, EL08; the jurisdiction's rules stay in code.

title: Wikipedia: Arc-fault circuit interrupter
summary: Describes arc-fault protection and dual-function devices combining it with ground-fault protection. Motivates EL07.

title: OSHA: Electrical - Overview
summary: OSHA's electrical overview states that electricity is a serious workplace hazard, that its standards protect employees from shock, electrocution, fires, and explosions, and that the most frequent causes of electrical injuries include contact with power lines, lack of ground-fault protection, a missing or discontinuous path to ground, equipment not used as prescribed, and improper use of extension and flexible cords. Motivates EL02 (hazard signs) and EL07 (ground-fault protection devices); the on-site electrician's determination governs.
